sections.h2: What stands between an Orange, NJ owner and a closing?
sections.html:
In the City of Orange Township, state law is not the only hurdle: the city code makes it unlawful to sell or transfer a residential property until a certificate of habitability is issued. Owner and buyer share responsibility for getting it, so plan for it at contract stage.

Orange covers 2.21 square miles in Essex County and has 35,642 residents by the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate, up from 34,447 at the 2020 census. That works out to more than 15,000 people per square mile. It borders East Orange, Glen Ridge, Montclair, South Orange and West Orange.

sections.h2: How did Orange grow, and what does that mean for the housing stock?
sections.html:
Orange began as part of Newark, was known as Newark Mountains, and adopted the name Orange in 1780. It separated as a township in 1806, was incorporated as a city in 1872 and switched back to township status in 1982. East Orange, South Orange and West Orange all split away from it in the 1860s.

The Morris and Essex Railroad reached the city in 1836, and the F. Berg & Co. hat factory building dates from 1907. Orange was a transport crossroads on the Newark and Mount Pleasant Turnpike long before it was a commuter suburb. For a seller, the practical point is that the inspection fee rises with the number of units, so owners of two- to five-unit buildings should read the fee schedule first.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Orange homeowners and renters?
sections.html:
Orange is a renter-majority city. Only 25.5 percent of housing units are owner-occupied, the median owner-occupied value is $365,500 and the median gross rent is $1,550. With three in four housing units renter-occupied, expect some buyers to be small landlords rather than owner-occupants.

sections.h2: What is a certificate of habitability, and how do I get one in Orange?
sections.html:
Chapter 156, Article VII of the city code requires a certificate of habitability, issued by the Division of Code Enforcement, before any residential property is sold, purchased, conveyed or transferred. The application is filed at 29 North Day Street, Room 305, and it must include a fully executed sales contract. The steps from the city's application are:

  • Check with the Building Division whether the property has open building permits, because all permits must be closed before a permanent certificate issues.
  • Complete the transaction information and attach the sales contract or deed.
  • Pay by certified check or money order made out to the City of Orange Township.
  • If the buyer is a company, supply its organization documents and a photo ID for the responsible member.
  • Schedule the fire certificate inspection with the Orange Fire Department.

Condominiums and townhouses skip this form and apply for a Certificate of Occupancy through the Building Division instead.

sections.h2: How much does the Orange certificate of habitability cost?
sections.html:
The fee depends on the number of units. The city's schedule lists $200 for a one-unit home, $300 for two units, $400 for three, $500 for four and $600 for five. Buildings with six to nine units pay $1,000. A second re-inspection costs $100 for a one-unit home. A missed appointment can trigger another inspection fee, so confirm access before the date.

Treat these as the schedule on the city's application and confirm the current figures with Code Enforcement before you write a check. Payment is only by certified check or money order.

sections.h2: Can I sell an Orange house as-is?
sections.html:
Yes, with conditions. If the contract calls for an as-is conveyance, the contract goes with the application and both owner and purchaser must sign it. If the inspection finds violations that cannot be fixed before closing, Code Enforcement may issue a temporary certificate of habitability, which is nonrenewable and good for no more than six months from the conveyance or possession date.

For a vacant or run-down house, the city's application asks for a letter from the buyer's attorney, signed by the buyer, acknowledging that permits must be obtained before renovations and that the property must stay unoccupied until a permanent certificate is granted.

The code exempts four kinds of transfer:

  • Transfers between immediate family members, including spouses.
  • A property certified within the previous six months.
  • A property bought to be demolished, after written notice to Code Enforcement and a demolition permit application.
  • A transfer by probate to heirs or beneficiaries under a will.

sections.h2: How do Orange property taxes and state fees affect my net?
sections.html:
Orange carries a heavy tax burden. In 2020 its equalized property tax rate was 4.679 percent, against 2.824 percent for Essex County and a 2.279 percent statewide average, which put it 12th highest in New Jersey. Buyers will compare your carrying costs with neighboring towns, so have recent bills ready.

The seller's Realty Transfer Fee is separate. The state's example lists $1,910 on a $325,000 deed with no exemption. The buyer's extra 1 percent fee starts above $1,000,000. Every deed needs a Gross Income Tax form too: the GIT/REP-3 for New Jersey residents, and GIT/REP-1 or GIT/REP-2 for nonresident sellers who must prepay. If you appeal an assessment, the Essex County board of taxation must receive the petition by April 1, or 45 days after notices are mailed if later.

sections.h2: How do Orange transit, roads and schools affect buyer demand?
sections.html:
Interstate 280 crosses the city from West Orange to East Orange, and Central Avenue is County Route 508. Valley Street, Lincoln Avenue, Scotland Road and Highland Avenue carry local traffic. The Orange and Highland Avenue stations on NJ Transit's Morris and Essex Lines reach Newark Broad Street, Secaucus Junction and New York Penn Station, and ten NJ Transit bus routes serve Newark and local trips.

The Orange Board of Education runs 12 schools and enrolled 5,629 students in 2020-21. It is one of 31 former Abbott districts, where the state pays all costs of school building projects. Schools include Rosa Parks Central Community School for grades 3 to 7, Orange Preparatory Academy for grades 8 and 9, Orange High School for grades 10 to 12 and the STEM Innovation Academy of the Oranges. The Orange Public Library, opened in 1901, holds about 200,000 volumes.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate of habitability to sell a house in Orange, NJ?
faqs.a: Yes. The city code makes it unlawful to sell or transfer residential property until the Division of Code Enforcement issues a certificate. Condominiums and townhouses use a Certificate of Occupancy application through the Building Division instead.

faqs.q: How much is the Orange certificate of habitability fee?
faqs.a: The application lists $200 for a one-unit property, $300 for two units, $400 for three, $500 for four and $600 for five. Pay by certified check or money order payable to the City of Orange Township, and confirm the current schedule with Code Enforcement.

faqs.q: Can a buyer take an Orange house with violations?
faqs.a: Sometimes. For an as-is sale, Code Enforcement may issue a temporary certificate of habitability valid for up to six months, and it cannot be renewed. The contract and a buyer's attorney letter go with the application.

faqs.q: Are any Orange transfers exempt from the certificate?
faqs.a: Yes. The code exempts transfers between immediate family members, properties certified in the previous six months, properties bought for demolition and probate transfers to heirs or beneficiaries under a will.

faqs.q: How does the high Orange tax rate affect a sale?
faqs.a: It affects what buyers will pay. The 2020 equalized rate was 4.679 percent, compared with 2.279 percent statewide. A seller who believes the assessment is too high can petition the Essex County board of taxation by April 1.
